stem.en: A clinic has two clear salt solutions, 0.9 % and 1.8 %. Both are uniform and both show no beam path. What is the difference between them?

text.en: Nothing. Both are salt in water, so either one can be used.
The concentration: each has a different mass of salt in every 100 mL of solution.
The size of the bottle: the 1.8 % bottle simply holds more liquid.
The temperature: the 1.8 % bottle has been kept warmer.

explanation.en: Both are solutions of the same salt, but 1.8 % has twice as much salt in every 100 mL. That is a difference in concentration. Option a is the idea this lesson corrects: being the same substances does not make two solutions the same. Option c fails because a percentage is about proportion, not about the size of the bottle.

hints.en: What does the number before the % sign tell you?
Would a small bottle of 1.8 % saline be weaker than a large bottle of 0.9 %?
